questions.question: Which set of components is required to fully specify a state‑space search problem as described in the material?

options.A: Initial state, actions, transition model, goal test, path‑cost function
options.B: Initial state and goal test only
options.C: Actions and a heuristic function only
options.D: Transition model and a depth limit only

questions.explanation:
The context lists these five elements (initial state, actions, transition model, goal test, path cost) as the essential parts of a search problem formulation [Page 13].

---

questions.question: In the 8‑puzzle example, each move of the blank tile has a cost of 1. If a solution requires 7 moves, what is the total path‑cost of that solution?
questions.explanation:
The path‑cost is defined as “1 per move” for the 8‑puzzle [Page 15]; thus 7 moves yield a cost of 7.

---

questions.question: According to the discussion of implementation, how does a “state” differ from a “node” in tree search?

options.A: A state represents a physical configuration, while a node is an occurrence of that state in the search tree together with bookkeeping information (parent, path cost, etc.)
options.B: A state includes the path cost, whereas a node does not
options.C: A node is the abstract representation of a problem, while a state is the concrete solution
options.D: There is no difference; the terms are used interchangeably

questions.explanation:
The text states that “A state is a (representation of) a physical configuration” and distinguishes it from nodes used in the search tree [Page 16].

---

questions.question: When formulating the Romania travel problem, which of the following correctly describes the goal test?

options.A: The agent has visited every city in Romania
options.B: The agent is currently located in Bucharest
options.C: The total travel cost is below a given threshold
options.D: The agent has returned to the starting city, Arad

questions.explanation:
The problem statement defines the goal as “be in Bucharest, Sgoal = {Bucharest}” [Page 13].

---

questions.question: Which of the following is *not* a requirement for a problem to be considered “well‑defined” in a state‑space search framework?
questions.explanation: A well‑defined problem must specify an initial state, actions, transition model, goal test, and path‑cost function; a heuristic is optional and not part of the formal definition [Page 13].
